hook.why: It opens on a question the audience already argues about — what should be added to Animal Hospital next — and answers it in the first line rather than teasing it. The gameplay is already running behind the pitch, so there is no title card and nothing to wait through.

scenes.action: A pink parent dog leads a small orange cat child, in a nappy and hoodie, in through the hospital entrance hallway.
scenes.dialogue: "What if we added kids to Animal Hospital?" / "WHAT IF WE ADDED KIDS TO ANIMAL HOSPITAL" (on-screen text)
scenes.camera: Eye-level medium, following the pair down the corridor
scenes.visual: Bright, clean low-poly hospital hallway; the two visitors read instantly against flat pale walls.

scenes.action: The pair arrive at the reception counter window and wait to be seen.
scenes.dialogue: "Parents would bring their children to the hospital" / "PARENTS WOULD BRING THEIR CHILDREN TO THE HOSPITAL" (on-screen text)
scenes.visual: Reception window with the counter framing the two characters.

scenes.action: A patient card is held up to camera, showing a photo and the name John John.
scenes.visual: The card fills the frame — the one moment the video stops moving so the detail registers.

scenes.action: A cut to the security booth, looking out at the waiting visitors.
scenes.camera: Interior wide from behind the booth glass
scenes.visual: Point-of-view shift to staff side, establishing the player's role in the loop.

scenes.action: A door marked with a baby-bottle icon opens onto a play area with a ball pit.
scenes.dialogue: "and if everything looks normal, they would be sent to a special kids room with toys and a ball pit" / "AND IF EVERYTHING LOOKS NORMAL" / "THEY WOULD BE SENT TO A SPECIAL KIDS ROOM" / "WITH TOYS AND A BALL PIT" (on-screen text)
scenes.visual: Saturated primary-coloured ball pit against the clean clinical palette — the brightest frame so far.

scenes.action: A green rabbit doctor in glasses and a moustache watches through a window as the cat toddler stands motionless, facing away from the toys.
scenes.dialogue: "But if you notice a child ignoring all the toys and strangely staring at the wall, be careful." / "BUT IF YOU NOTICE A CHILD" / "IGNORING ALL THE TOYS" (on-screen text)
scenes.visual: The stillness is the story — everything else in frame has been moving until now.

scenes.action: The camera cuts to the front of the child, revealing distorted reptilian eyes and a jagged mouth as an anomaly alarm pulses.
scenes.dialogue: "That means it's actually an anomaly." / "AND STRANGELY STARING AT THE WALL" / "BE CAREFUL THAT MEANS IT'S ACTUALLY AN ANOMALY" (on-screen text)
scenes.camera: Push to close-up on the face, held
scenes.visual: The reveal: familiar toddler geometry with wrong eyes and mouth, lit by a pulsing warning.

scenes.action: The rabbit doctor enters carrying a grey tablet and walks it over to the child.
scenes.dialogue: "Grab the tablet and walk up to the child with it." / "GRAB THE TABLET AND WALK UP" / "TO THE CHILD WITH IT" (on-screen text)
scenes.camera: Medium tracking the doctor into the room
scenes.visual: The solution is a prop the viewer can picture holding — a plain grey tablet.

scenes.action: The child takes the tablet and its face instantly reverts to normal large glossy eyes as it plays.
scenes.dialogue: "The anomaly will immediately turn back into a normal kid." / "ROBLOX" / "THE ANOMALY WILL IMMEDIATELY TURN BACK" / "INTO A NORMAL KID" (on-screen text)
scenes.camera: Close-up, matching the reveal framing so the change reads as a swap
scenes.visual: Same frame as the anomaly shot with the face corrected — the joke is that Roblox itself is the cure.

scenes.action: The child and parents walk out happily past the doctor, with a thumbs-up graphic overlaid.
scenes.dialogue: "Leave a like if you want this update." / "LEAVE A LIKE IF YOU WANT THIS UPDATE" (on-screen text)
scenes.camera: Medium-wide, pulling back to the corridor that opened the video
scenes.visual: Closes on the entrance hallway it started in, so the last frame reads as the first.
